Question: What is your idea of a perfect relationship or a perfect marriage?
Old_Answer: An old, experienced man was traveling on a train. In the same compartment, a couple was also traveling. They were in their early 40s. At every station, small or big, the man got down from the train and got something for the woman - Coffee, fruit, chocolate, cookies, etc. Even though the woman denied eating, the man persuaded her to have them. The older man was observing everything, and then he asked the woman about her relationship with the man at one station when he got down searching for something. "Who is he?" He asked. "He is my husband." She answered. "No, he is not your husband." The older man replied. "Why? How can you say that?" She felt a little bothered. "A husband will never do so much. You are telling a lie." The older man smiled. The woman found some affection in his smile and confessed that he was not her husband but her husband's friend who was in love with her. While telling the truth, she blushed, and the happiness on her face was quite visible. This is a story, and I am sure many of you can relate to the statement that a husband will never do so much. Because, at some point in time, marriages lose their charm. The spouses take each other for granted. Getting attention from your partner seems like a dream. That's why I mentioned once that marriages should come with expiry dates. Suppose it has to expire in the next year, then the spouses will do their best to keep the relationship alive if there is a dependency from any side. They will long for the renewal of the marriage at any cost, and for that, they will try to keep their spouse happy and content. Then, no need to have a boyfriend or girlfriend from outside. What a great idea! No? Think about it. We are so conditioned by society that we cannot think of anything beyond the cultural norms. P.S.- this write up is not to glorify the extra marital affair but it talks about an idea of keeping the relationship/marriage lively for a lifetime. By the way, that older man was no one but Osho.😊 Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Partners should feel safe to express their thoughts and feelings without the fear of judgment. This creates a space where both individuals can grow and evolve, both as a couple and as individuals. Trust is another crucial element. When you trust your partner, you can be vulnerable, share your dreams, and even your fears, knowing they will be there to lift you up. I’ve learned that a perfect relationship also involves compromise. It’s about finding a balance between your needs and your partner’s, understanding that both are equally important. Additionally, shared values and goals can strengthen the bond, as they provide a common direction to work towards. However, it’s essential to maintain individuality; a perfect marriage allows both partners to pursue their passions and interests while supporting each other. Lastly, laughter and joy should be woven into the fabric of the relationship. Finding humor in everyday situations can lighten the load during tough times. In essence, a perfect relationship is not devoid of challenges but is characterized by the ability to face them together, fostering a deep connection that withstands the test of time. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Question: I am so alone. I am depressed and lonely and have no friends or significant other. What is wrong with me that makes me so lonely in life?
Old_Answer: For the last two days, I have been feeling like you. I was down in the dumps and had no one to share my feelings with. The more I craved someone with whom I could share my pain freely, the more I felt stifled. "I am no one's priority. No one is concerned about my well-being. There is no one to enquire if I have eaten food or slept well." this thought made me sicker. I hardly ate or drank water. I suffered from insomnia, and during office hours, I dozed off. I felt too fragile even to walk. Out of exasperation, I got furious with a little mistake of my child, yelled at him, and ended up with shedding tears. My sister from far away sensed my despairs and called me to know how I was doing. I enthusiastically exaggerated the taste of chicken soup that I had recently cooked for my child. She couldn't guess what I was going through. This is how a depressed person acts. I felt like consulting a psychiatrist this morning because my depression doesn't seem to fade. Most of the time, I am bright, chirpy, and upbeat, but occasionally, I am clutched by low spirits. And life feels static and pointless. However, in the afternoon, I picked up a storybook by Ruskin Bond and started reading it. After reading a few pages, I felt a little stable. And then, I took the chance to analyze my life, past experiences, desires, and needs. "What is the guarantee that someone (if I find one) will keep me happy?" I asked myself. In the last four years, I have worked very hard to regain my mental peace which I can't ruin by giving someone else the remote control of my life. I have seen people who brutally walked out from my life without giving notice. Come on! I can't make the same mistake. I will work on myself. I am already in love with my aloneness and a bit of loneliness - I will convert it into fulfilling solitude. If I have taken responsibility for my life, I will ensure it is more gratifying. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Start by acknowledging your feelings; it’s okay to feel this way. Then, consider taking small steps to engage with the world around you. Remember, loneliness does not define you; it’s a feeling that can change. You are worthy of love and friendship, and with time and effort, you can find your tribe. It’s a journey, but every step counts. Thank you for sharing your feelings. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Question: What should I do if I heard people start gossiping about me?
Old_Answer: Recently, I heard something that made me split my sides. A relative told my mother what other relatives said about me. When I divorced my husband, they spread the rumor that I had an affair and would marry that guy after my divorce. Four years have passed since the separation, and I am still single. However, in these four years, my life became more stable; I gained more freedom, happiness, and peace and established myself as an author. The imaginary guy my relatives saw in their dreams didn't meet me yet, and I am sure he wouldn't ever meet me. Because my taste differs from my relatives, I will definitely not like a guy of their choice and imagination. So I laugh. I enjoy their gossip. And have fun with their rumors. Because I prefer to work on my aspirations rather than pay attention to the blabber of others. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.
Answer_with_writing_sample: When you hear people gossiping about you, it can feel like a punch to the gut. I remember a time in my life when I was the subject of whispers and speculation. It was during a challenging phase, and I felt exposed and vulnerable. The first thing I did was take a step back and breathe. I realized that gossip often stems from insecurity or misunderstanding. Instead of reacting impulsively, I chose to reflect on the situation. Ask yourself, "What is the truth?" and "Do these opinions define who I am?" It’s crucial to remember that people will talk, but their words do not hold power over your self-worth. I found strength in surrounding myself with supportive friends who uplifted me and reminded me of my value. If the gossip is hurtful and persistent, consider addressing it directly with those involved. A calm conversation can sometimes clear the air and dispel misconceptions. However, if the gossip continues, it may be best to distance yourself from those who engage in it. Protect your peace. Focus on your goals and passions, and let your actions speak louder than the words of others. Ultimately, the most important opinion about you is your own. Embrace who you are, flaws and all, and let that confidence shine through. Remember, you are not alone in this; many have faced similar challenges and emerged stronger. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Question: As a woman, what do some men do that creeps you out?
Old_Answer: Years ago, I was travelling on a train. My co-passengers in my compartment were homely people. There was an old man and his wife, two middle-aged men and a bright young man who was a probationary officer in a bank. Since the journey was nearly 36 hours long, we got along well. The old man liked me for my thoughts and wanted to talk to me more and more. The bank officer grew interested when I shared my opinion on a few topics. The bank officer and I were almost of the same age so we became friends. We shared our Facebook account and he picked up some of my stylish pictures and sent me on WhatsApp commenting something funny but decent. I liked him. He had a great sense of humour. We made fun of everyone on the train through messages and giggled. When we reached our destination, we both exchanged our numbers. At this time, I had grown weary of my monotonous married life though it was just a year old. I really needed someone who could make me laugh. I began to talk to him every day during our office hours. Every day he asked me with care if I had my food on time. I was always smiling and shared the secret of this smile with my husband too. However, slowly, that young man started showing me a different aspect of his personality. He sounded cheap in his talks. His jokes turned obscene and the messages seemed ugly which forced me to block him everywhere. “You need to be careful”, said my husband later. Some men are real creeps. Or I can say, they tend to mistake the inclination that a woman has for them. They walk with a mask on their face which doesn't impress me. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

It’s not just the comments; it’s the way they make you feel like a target rather than a person. Another behavior that creeps me out is when men refuse to take no for an answer. I once had a colleague who persistently pursued me despite my clear disinterest. His insistence made me feel trapped, as if my boundaries were irrelevant to him. Additionally, the use of social media can amplify this creepiness. I’ve received messages from men I barely know, making inappropriate remarks or asking personal questions that feel invasive. It’s alarming how some men think they can bypass social norms simply because they’re behind a screen. Lastly, there’s the subtle manipulation, where some men try to guilt-trip women into spending time with them or engaging in activities they’re uncomfortable with. This kind of behavior not only creeps me out but also makes me question their respect for my autonomy. It’s crucial for men to understand that their actions can have a profound impact on women’s comfort and safety. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Question: Do Indian parents give smartphones to their children at a young age? If so, why?
Old_Answer: I gave a smartphone to my child when he was eight months old. It sounds weird, but I had no choice. He was not good at eating, and I struggled to feed him every day. I have been a working mother and have always been in a rush. All the passersby knew this adamant child as I fed him, making him sit on the wall near the main gate and showing him dogs and cows. I had hired an adult girl as a caretaker who used to feed him in my absence. It was chaos for that girl as well to feed him every time. However, I noticed he could easily take the first few spoons while watching YouTube videos. That eased our task to some extent. So I permanently gave my smartphone to him and bought a new one for myself. He watched videos while having food until the last year. Now, he watches TV or laptop. I have banned the mobile for him. You can blame me for being an irresponsible mother, but I was helpless. He needed some diversion to swallow the morsel; otherwise, he threw it out. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.
Answer_with_writing_sample: Yes, Indian parents often give smartphones to their children at a young age, and there are several reasons behind this trend. In today's digital age, smartphones have become an integral part of our lives, serving not just as communication tools but also as gateways to education and entertainment. Many parents believe that providing their children with smartphones can enhance their learning experience. With access to educational apps, online resources, and e-books, children can explore subjects beyond their school curriculum. However, the decision is not solely based on educational benefits. In many cases, parents feel the need to stay connected with their children, especially in urban areas where safety concerns are prevalent. A smartphone allows parents to track their child's whereabouts and maintain communication, providing a sense of security. Additionally, peer pressure plays a significant role; as more children in a social circle own smartphones, parents may feel compelled to provide one to their child to avoid feelings of exclusion. However, this trend comes with its own set of challenges. Many parents struggle to monitor their children's screen time and online activities, leading to concerns about exposure to inappropriate content and social media pressures. Ultimately, while smartphones can offer numerous advantages, it is crucial for parents to strike a balance between connectivity and ensuring their child's well-being. As a single mother, I understand the complexities of parenting in a digital world, and I believe that open communication about technology use is essential for fostering a healthy relationship with smartphones. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Question: What are some small things that you miss the most in your life?
Old_Answer: My father adored me when I was a little girl. He was so fond of me that he wanted to see me as soon as he returned from his clinic. He would scoop me into his arms, planting a tender kiss on my forehead, tousling my hair and gently rubbing his chin against mine. At night, he would cradle me and we’d playfully roll in bed, creating moments filled with laughter. This was the love he showered on me during the childhood. “I love her the most” He proudly declared to everyone, expressing his deep affection for me. I cherish those beautiful moments the most in my life. Yesterday, my mother conveyed over the phone that he no longer wishes to travel to Bangalore. He says his body no longer supports extensive journeys; he is now 76. I feel a profound sadness, thinking how things change in our life. He is sacrificing his fondness for his daughter and grandson due to his weakened body. And I am struggling to accept this reality. I miss my father, his love and his fondness. I yearn for those gentle kisses, surprising tickles and daily hugs. I miss him a lot! Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Question: What do you think is the easy way that leads us to heaven?
Old_Answer: My grandfather (paternal) was a religious man. He went on several pilgrimages. He never touched non-vegetarian food in his life. He never missed any fast for Ekadashi, which is considered the most auspicious fast in the Hindu religion.
